clue.text: It can be of assistance when one is going up the wall

definitions.text: It can be of assistance when one is going up the wall

parts.words: It can be of assistance when one is going up the wall
parts.note: going up the wall sounds like losing one's temper, but read literally it is climbing a wall, where a folding ladder helps

explanation.surface: Something that helps when you are going crazy with frustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going up the wall' is the idiom for becoming furious; the clue asks you to take it literally, as climbing beside a wall to paint or mend it.
explanation.definitionFit: A folding ladder with flat treads is what a decorator stands on to climb a wall.

clue.text: Sort of work one cannot do alone

definitions.text: Sort of work one cannot do alone

parts.words: Sort of work one cannot do alone
parts.note: the clue describes a kind of work that by its nature needs several people pulling together

explanation.surface: A job description that demands colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: The word combines with 'work' to give the familiar compound for cooperative effort, which no single person can manage.
explanation.definitionFit: Teamwork is joint effort by a group, so the group is the sort of work needing others.

clue.text: Pound Pete's exchange with another pound

indicators.note: Pete's letters exchange places with one another, a cue to rearrange them

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Pete swaps one pound coin for another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchange' rearranges PETES together with L (pound) to give the answer; the first 'Pound' is the verb, to crush or grind.
explanation.definitionFit: A pestle is the club-shaped tool used to grind or crush things in a mortar, so it pounds.

clue.text: Give an explanation of the story

definitions.meaning: to ... for something is to explain it
a narrative or report of events

explanation.definitionFit: To account for is to explain, and an account is also a narrative report of events.

clue.text: Board of trade

definitions.meaning: softwood timber, a plank of pine or fir

explanation.definitionFit: Deal is pine or fir planking, and a deal is also a business bargain or transaction.

clue.text: In poor health as a result of an accident?

definitions.text: as a result of an accident?
definitions.meaning: knocked over by a vehicle in a road accident

explanation.definitionFit: Someone exhausted and sickly is said to be run-down, and a pedestrian hit by a car has literally been run down.

clue.text: I'm game but cannot wait with this

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
patience is a card game played alone, called solitaire in America

explanation.surface: Someone keen to play a card game who is too restless to wait.
explanation.walkthrough: PATIENCE is the British name for solitaire, the one-player card game; the irony is that its name is the very quality the restless player lacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Restlessness at delay is the feeling that makes a person unable to wait.

clue.text: Concerned but not impartial

definitions.meaning: taking an interest, curious or involved
having a stake in the outcome, biased

explanation.definitionFit: An engaged person is concerned, and a party with a stake in the result is not impartial, as in an interested party.

clue.text: Topless ladies-a sign of what is to come

definitions.text: a sign of what is to come

indicators.note: topless means the word loses its top, its first letter

parts.note: ladies are women

explanation.surface: Seeing ladies without tops is taken as a portent of the future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' removes the first letter, W, from WOMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent is an event taken as a sign of something about to happen.

clue.text: Cad is in hay playing with a string of flowers

indicators.note: the letters are playing about, a sign that they get rearranged

explanation.surface: A cad romps in the hay with a garland of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges the letters CADISINHAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A daisy-chain is a garland made by threading daisy stalks together, so a string of blooms.

clue.text: Indisposed sea-dog's medicine?

indicators.note: something indisposed is out of order, so these letters are put back in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the hyphen and the possessive

explanation.surface: An ailing old sailor needs his medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indisposed' looks like the sailor's illness but tells you to rearrange SEADOG. The question mark marks the definition as loose: the answer is an amount of medicine rather than medicine itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A dose or measured quantity of a drug is the medicine one takes at a time.

clue.text: Show attendant a set of books

parts.note: a page is a young attendant at court or a wedding
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A display of a servant reading a collection of books.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is an elaborate public spectacle or procession, a show.

clue.text: What an aggressive manager will do for a boxer

definitions.text: What an aggressive manager will do for a boxer

parts.words: What an aggressive manager will do for a boxer
parts.note: a combative boss provokes quarrels, but a boxer's manager literally chooses an opponent and arranges a bout

explanation.surface: A belligerent boss's behaviour, or a fight manager's job.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means to start a quarrel deliberately; a boxing manager does it literally by selecting the bout.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately provoking a quarrel is the idiom; literally, selecting a bout is a boxing manager's task.

clue.text: A birdie or one better in the valleys of course

indicators.note: the bird goes in the valleys, placed inside that word

parts.note: glens are narrow Scottish valleys
an eagle is a bird, and in golf it is one stroke better than a birdie, two under par

explanation.surface: A golf score of birdie or better scored on a course among valleys.
explanation.walkthrough: GLENEAGLES is a famous golf resort in Perthshire, Scotland; 'of course' is a golfing pun, since birdie and eagle are golf scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Gleneagles is a celebrated Scottish golf links that has hosted the Ryder Cup.

clue.text: Large cask is in North Africa

definitions.note: the definition names a place found in North Africa, the capital of Tunisia

parts.note: a tun is a large barrel for wine or beer

explanation.surface: A big barrel sits somewhere in North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunis is the capital city of Tunisia, on the North African coast.

clue.text: Deceive twice almost

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: twice is two times

explanation.surface: Cheating on someone very nearly twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter, S, from TWO TIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: To two-time is to be unfaithful to a partner by secretly seeing someone else, a kind of betrayal.

clue.text: One of the top men in the building industry

definitions.text: One of the top men in the building industry

parts.words: One of the top men in the building industry
parts.note: top men suggests senior executives, but here it means workers who are literally at the top, on the roof

explanation.surface: A leading executive in construction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top men' suggests bosses; the roof-covering worker is a top man only because he works on the highest part of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofer laying slates or tiles works on the uppermost part of a building.

clue.text: I go round an Italian city

indicators.note: the word for go is placed round the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a turn at a game

explanation.surface: I tour around a city in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go round' looks like one phrase meaning travel around; split it so 'go' gives TURN and 'round' puts it around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a major city in Piedmont, north-west Italy.

clue.text: Sign on the staff

parts.note: staff suggests employees, but in music the staff is the set of five lines on which notes are written

explanation.surface: An instruction to enlist the employees, or a notice for workers.
explanation.walkthrough: The staff, or stave, is the five-line grid of written music, and this symbol sits at its start to fix the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A clef is the symbol at the start of a musical stave showing the pitch of the notes.

clue.text: Water rate

parts.note: suggests a household bill for the water supply, but means a speed measured on water

explanation.surface: A utility charge for water.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the water rate was a household charge for water supply; here it is a unit of speed at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot is one nautical mile per hour, the speed measure used by ships.

clue.text: Duck down

parts.note: reads as an order to crouch, but means the soft feathers of a duck, used to fill quilts

explanation.surface: An instruction to crouch out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird gives its name to a quilt stuffed with its soft breast feathers, the eiderdown.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a sea duck whose soft breast feathers are prized for stuffing quilts.

clue.text: Lakes 'e'd transformed in the Lake District

definitions.note: the definition names a valley found within the Lake District, the hill region of north-west England

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: He changed the lakes in England's Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' rearranges LAKESED; 'e'd is a dropped-aitch 'he'd'. The Lake District is a mountainous national park in Cumbria.
explanation.definitionFit: Eskdale is a valley in western Cumbria, within the Lake District national park.

clue.text: Negotiate again for a withdrawal

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to treat is to negotiate terms, as in treat with the enemy

explanation.surface: Reopening talks in order to pull back troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Negotiate again' gives TREAT preceded by RE; to 'treat with' someone is an old phrase for negotiating.
explanation.definitionFit: A military pull-back from a position is a retreat.

clue.text: Being ever youthful, geta leg up in choppy seas

indicators.note: the reversed limb goes in the shuffled sea letters
choppy water is rough and broken, so the letters are rearranged
in a down clue up would mean upwards; here it reads the word backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A youthful person gets a boost from rough seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LEG into GEL, which goes 'in' AESS, a rearrangement of SEAS signalled by 'choppy'. 'get a' is a link; the printed 'geta' is a misprint for 'get a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who never seems to grow older is ageless, timelessly young.

clue.text: Communist leader or a pretty girl perhaps

parts.note: a Red is a communist
a head is a leader or chief

explanation.surface: A Communist Party leader, or alternatively a pretty young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The question of whether 'pretty' suits the answer is the setter's joke; the 'perhaps' marks a girl as one example of such a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with auburn or ginger hair, often a girl in old crossword parlance, is so called.

clue.text: Distinction for being on in time

indicators.note: on sits in the word for time, inside it

parts.note: an hour is a period of time

explanation.surface: An award for always being punctual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on in time' reads as punctuality, a red herring: 'in' is the container signal, and 'for being' merely links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An honour is an award or mark of distinction, such as a knighthood.

clue.text: Girl riding in a storm

indicators.note: a storm throws things into disorder, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl rides out in bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a storm' rearranges RIDING.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrid is a female first name, as in the actress Ingrid Bergman.

clue.text: Over 501

definitions.meaning: five hundred written as the Roman numeral D, followed by the number one spelt out in words

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a numeral to be read in a mixed style: Roman for the hundreds, a spelt-out word for the units. 501 is also the starting score in darts, a deliberate distraction.
explanation.definitionFit: When something is over it is finished, and 501 read as Roman five hundred plus a written one spells the same letters.

clue.text: Does this work cause worry?

parts.note: the word means to worry, and joined to work it names decorative cutwork in thin wood

explanation.surface: A question whether a job is stressful.
explanation.walkthrough: Fretwork is ornamental openwork cut in wood with a fine saw; the word on its own means worry.
explanation.definitionFit: To fret is to be anxious, and fretwork is ornamental carved openwork.

clue.text: Chairman's position is described as fair

definitions.meaning: literally, over the board of directors he chairs

explanation.definitionFit: A chairman sits over the board of directors, and an honest, open deal is also called legitimate this way.

clue.text: Rotter might be downtrodden

definitions.meaning: the back part of the foot or shoe, literally trodden down

explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel is a heel, and the rear of the foot or shoe is literally trodden down with each step.

clue.text: Choose to speak for the voters

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote
to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: Picking someone to address the voting public.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole body of people entitled to vote in an election.
